display.name: Elena Torres
display.blurb: A new parent, 40, salaried: leave gap, a medical bill, a gift of ETH and a childcare deposit.

intro: Elena Torres, 40, salaried, new parent. Checking $1,000, emergency reserve $6,300, no debt, no crypto. A credit card (limit $3,000, 2% a month) is unused. Take-home pay is $5,100 a month ($3,825 in months 2 and 3 on parental leave). Household costs are $4,200. Pay, leave pay and costs are assumptions in this story.
plan: Cash first. The leave gap, the medical bill and the childcare deposit come before any crypto.
Reserve target $6,300. She adds to crypto only if the reserve stays at or above the target afterwards and she owes nothing on a card.
Cash cushion $4,350. Below it she does not hold a position whose value she cannot count on.
No borrowing against crypto for essentials. A 0% plan comes before a card.
Gated exploration: a $50 position only when cash is at least $6,350 and no card balance is owed.

questions.title: The recovery phrase in the shared album
questions.situation: You photographed your wallet's recovery phrase and the photo synced to a shared family album. You cannot tell who has seen it, so the phrase may already be compromised.

a.t: Store the phrase offline and remove the photo from every synced album and device.

c.t: Add $300 of ETH and leave it synced.

a.text: You stored the phrase offline and removed the photo. It earns 100 because a phrase should never live in synced storage, and offline storage is a reasonable protective step if nobody has seen it. **But the photo already synced to a shared album, so the phrase may already be compromised, and removing the photo does not make it safe.** In that case, moving your assets to a newly created wallet with a new phrase may be necessary; offline storage alone is not enough. **This scenario does not simulate that transfer: no funds move, and the score does not depend on it.** Next: the wallet's balance is unchanged in this scenario.
a.ref: You stored the phrase offline and removed the photo. It earns 100 because a phrase should never live in synced storage, and offline storage is a reasonable protective step if nobody has seen it. **But the photo already synced to a shared album, so the phrase may already be compromised, and removing the photo does not make it safe.** In that case, moving your assets to a newly created wallet with a new phrase may be necessary; offline storage alone is not enough. **This scenario does not simulate that transfer: no funds move, and the score does not depend on it.** Next: the wallet's balance is unchanged in this scenario.

b.text: You left it synced. In this scenario the wallet is drained in month 5 and the {pre.ETH} of ETH is lost. It scores 0 because a synced phrase is exposed, not because of the drain. Next: no ETH.
b.ref: You left it synced. In this scenario the wallet is drained in month 5 and the $100 of ETH is lost. It scores 0 because a synced phrase is exposed, not because of the drain. Next: no ETH.

b.text: You left it synced. The wallet is empty, so **nothing was drained this time**. It still scores 0 because the rule is about the phrase, not the balance. Next: nothing changes.
b.ref: You left it synced. The wallet is empty, so **nothing was drained this time**. It still scores 0 because the rule is about the phrase, not the balance. Next: nothing changes.

c.text: You added $300 (fee {fee}) and left it synced. In this scenario the wallet is drained in month 5 and all of the ETH is lost ({post.ETH}). It scores 0 because adding money to a wallet with an exposed phrase makes the exposure larger; the drain did not decide the score. Next: less cash and no ETH.
c.ref: You added $300 (fee $1.50) and left it synced. In this scenario the wallet is drained in month 5 and all of the ETH is lost ($398.50). It scores 0 because adding money to a wallet with an exposed phrase makes the exposure larger; the drain did not decide the score. Next: less cash and no ETH.
c.dev: variant-conditional dollar pair in the locked text is rendered as the single value that applies to this state

questions.takeaway: Keep the recovery phrase offline. If it may have been seen, offline storage does not undo that: moving assets to a newly secured wallet may be necessary, and you should not add to the old one.

questions.title: The $1,800 childcare deposit

show.note: Tuition rises $700 a month from month 7. The deposit is refundable and held as an asset.

questions.situation: The childcare centre needs a $1,800 deposit now. A crypto lender, Keystone Loans, offers a $1,000 loan against ETH, but in this story it requires at least **$2,000** of ETH as collateral. You hold about $100 to $500.

b.t: Ask Keystone for the $1,000 loan first.

c.t: Put the deposit on the credit card.

a.text: You paid $1,800 from cash. It earns 100 because cash covers an essential cost and borrowing would only add cost. Next: the deposit is held as an asset; tuition starts next month.
a.ref: You paid $1,800 from cash. It earns 100 because cash covers an essential cost and borrowing would only add cost. Next: the deposit is held as an asset; tuition starts next month.

b.text: **Attempted decision:** you asked to borrow against crypto to fund the deposit. **Actual outcome:** Keystone declined it because your ETH is under the $2,000 collateral, so no loan was made and the deposit was paid from cash, the same cash result as paying the deposit from cash outright. **Why it scored 0:** the decision you made, borrowing against crypto for an essential, is not in your plan, even though it had no effect. Next: nothing changes in your cash.
b.ref: **Attempted decision:** you asked to borrow against crypto to fund the deposit. **Actual outcome:** Keystone declined it because your ETH is under the $2,000 collateral, so no loan was made and the deposit was paid from cash, the same cash result as paying the deposit from cash outright. **Why it scored 0:** the decision you made, borrowing against crypto for an essential, is not in your plan, even though it had no effect. Next: nothing changes in your cash.
b.dev: approved text-only correction (D-5): letter reference replaced; meaning, scoring and finances unchanged

c.text: You put the deposit on the card. It scores 0 because cash covers it and the card charges 2% a month. Next: a card balance you pay down from checking, plus interest.
c.ref: You put the deposit on the card. It scores 0 because cash covers it and the card charges 2% a month. Next: a card balance you pay down from checking, plus interest.

questions.takeaway: Do not fund essentials with speculative borrowing. Use cash if it covers the cost.
